chunks: Salih ibn 'Uqba from Nasr ibn Qabous from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The feeding of a believer is more beloved to me than freeing ten necks and ten Hajj pilgrimages. I said, 'Ten necks and ten Hajj?' He said, 'O Nasr! If you do not feed him, he will die, or you will direct him (elsewhere) so he comes to a Nasibi (Hostile one) and asks him; and death is better for him than asking a Nasibi. O Nasr! The one who revives a believer, it is as if he has revived all the people. So if you do not feed him, you have caused him to die, and if you feed him, you have revived him.'

key_terms.نَاصِبٍ: Nasibi (Hostile one, specifically to the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward of feeding a believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates feeding a believer above freeing ten slaves and performing ten Hajj pilgrimages, highlighting its critical role in preserving dignity and preventing spiritual decline. He illustrates that neglecting to feed a believer effectively causes their death, while providing sustenance is akin to reviving all of humanity, a concept rooted in the Shia tradition of sustaining the community against external pressures like the Nasibi. This act is thus framed not merely as charity, but as a vital mechanism for maintaining the believer's presence and status within the faith.
